document_title: UA regents moved the AI vote. Campus policies start first.
post_copy:
In May, UA regents asked for a system AI statement. In November, they put campus AI policies ahead of the vote on it.

UA IT chief Ben Shier says about 20 percent of his first draft survived human edits. He wrote it by prompting Claude.

Next month. UAA's Faculty Senate parked its vote to reject and replace AI Engaged until then.
February. Regents vote on a statement that sets no policy but would require one at each of the three universities.
Adoption. Only then does a one-year clock start for a system-wide AI policy report.

Campus rules get a head start on the document meant to frame them.

The deck opens on the moved vote, then what AI Engaged is, Shier's 20 percent estimate, the Anchorage dissent and a map of the new order.

In February, will regents be setting direction or signing off on rules the campuses already started?

#UniversityOfAlaska #AIPolicy #AlaskaHigherEd

slides.headline: Campus policies start first.
slides.body: Regents pushed the AI vote to February.

slides.headline: The vote moved. The work didn't.
slides.body: Meeting at UAF, regents postponed AI Engaged to their February meeting and told the AI Coordinating Council to start campus-specific AI policies in the interim, ADN reports.

slides.headline: A benchmark, not a law.
slides.body: AI Engaged is a four-page statement of intent, ADN reports. It doesn't establish policy.

slides.headline: About 20 percent survived, Shier says.
slides.body: Ben Shier, UA's chief information technology officer, wrote the first draft by prompting Claude with human ideas, "all fed to Claude." He says about 20 percent of that two-page draft survived human edits.

slides.headline: Nearly 200 students and staff asked for a brief statement written by humans.
UAA's Faculty Senate paused too.
slides.body: Senators postponed their vote on a resolution to reject and replace AI Engaged until next month, ADN reports. Senate chair Andrea Dewees said, "I think it's probably going to be messy."

slides.headline: Campus policies start before the statement.
slides.body: The statement would require each of the three universities to write its own AI policy. That work now starts first. A one-year clock for a system-wide policy report starts only at adoption.
labels: One year to a system policy report

slides.headline: The rules get drawn campus by campus.
slides.body: UA says the statement keeps curriculum, academic integrity and faculty instructional judgment with UAA, UAF and UAS. Cooper says UA is "never going to have everyone on the same page with AI."

slides.headline: Campus rules first, or statement first?
slides.body: Which order should UA have chosen? Say so in the comments.

editor_notes_for_email: This edition is an UPDATE of No.109 (November 8th), which shipped before the vote outcome was confirmed. The caption is carried byte for byte with no factual flags, and the 20 percent figure is Shier's own estimate, attributed to him on the caption and on slide 4. The UA board site (alaska.edu/bor) returned HTTP 503, so the postponement rests on ADN (November 12th) and KTUU (November 9th), which reported it independently, and no primary record of the action was reachable. The UAA senate's "next month" is printed on the slides as DECEMBER, PER ADN, and the November 5th faculty rebuttal op-ed and ADN October 4th are left out of the sources because no claim the deck uses rests on them.
